therapy_note: Puriya Dhanashri is one of the most emotionally rich raags in the entire system. It combines the serious teevra Ma of the Poorvi family with komal Re, komal Dha, and shuddh Ga and Ni — creating a sound that is simultaneously yearning and resolved. It is a sandhiprakash (twilight) raag — like twilight itself, it holds two qualities at once: the ending of one thing and the beginning of another.

notes_for_vocalist: The three critical corrections vs. common errors: Ga is SHUDDH (not komal), Dha is KOMAL (not shuddh), Ni is SHUDDH (not komal). Getting even one of these wrong makes this sound like a different raag entirely. The teevra Ma is essential — never use shuddh Ma in this raag. Ga (shuddh) is the vadi and should be sung with full, tender weight. This raag is for experienced singers — its emotional complexity requires equivalent musical maturity.
common_mistakes: Treating Ga as komal — Ga is SHUDDH in Puriya Dhanashri
Treating Dha as shuddh — Dha is KOMAL here
Treating Ni as komal — Ni is SHUDDH here
Using shuddh Ma — only teevra Ma is permitted
Confusing with Poorvi or Shree, which share some notes
variant_notes: Some gharanas and musicologists describe slight variations in Pa's treatment — it may be alpatva (weak) in some renditions. Vadi-samvadi assignment can vary by source.
